MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Models.Relics.EmberTe.reason: Backing field for a private per-instance combat counter/flag on a RelicModel subclass whose setter -- directly, or via a private UpdateDisplay()/CheckIfUsedUp()/RefreshCounter() helper, or (Pocketwatch/VelvetChoker) via plain field increments in the hook method immediately followed by such a helper call -- additionally fires RelicModel.DisplayAmountChanged (RelicModel.cs:468-471) and/or writes RelicModel.Status (RelicModel.cs:330-345) and/or `base.DynamicVars[key].BaseValue`. Every UpdateDisplay()/CheckIfUsedUp() implementation checked (Kunai, Kusarigama, LetterOpener, Metronome, Nunchaku, OrnamentalFan, Shuriken, TuningFork, IronClub, GalacticDust, SilverCrucible) does nothing beyond reading DynamicVars for a threshold comparison, writing base.Status, and calling InvokeDisplayAmountChanged -- no gameplay-affecting logic. DisplayAmountChanged has exactly two consumers in the whole codebase, NPower and NRelicInventoryHolder (both Godot UI nodes) -- bypassing it during a restore skips nothing but a counter-badge refresh. Status and DynamicVars are independently captured per-relic in RelicCapture (StateSnapshot.cs:149-155, populated at :641-654 from the same relic instance in the same loop iteration that also takes its Shadow()) and explicitly restored by RestoreRelicStates ahead of the raw field sweep (StateSnapshot.cs:1149-1152, before the CopyMutableFields(Shadow(shadow), r.Ref) call at :1161) -- so even though the raw copy never re-runs this setter's Status/DynamicVars-mirroring logic, both of those already got the correct snapshot-time value through their own dedicated path (see the RelicModel._status/StackCount/IsWax/IsMelted entries above), and can never end up inconsistent with this counter's own restored value, which was captured from the exact same relic instance at the exact same instant. Every UpdateDisplay()/CheckIfUsedUp() implementation checked (Kunai, Kusarigama, LetterOpener, Metronome, Nunchaku, OrnamentalFan, Shuriken, TuningFork, IronClub, GalacticDust, SilverCrucible) does nothing beyond reading DynamicVars for a threshold comparison, writing base.Status, and calling InvokeDisplayAmountChanged -- no gameplay-affecting logic. DisplayAmountChanged has exactly two consumers in the whole codebase, NPower and NRelicInventoryHolder (both Godot UI nodes) -- bypassing it during a restore skips nothing but a counter-badge refresh. Status and DynamicVars are independently captured per-relic in RelicCapture (StateSnapshot.cs:149-155, populated at :641-654 from the same relic instance in the same loop iteration that also takes its Shadow()) and explicitly restored by RestoreRelicStates ahead of the raw field sweep (StateSnapshot.cs:1149-1152, before the CopyMutableFields(Shadow(shadow), r.Ref) call at :1161) -- so even though the raw copy never re-runs this setter's Status/DynamicVars-mirroring logic, both of those already got the correct snapshot-time value through their own dedicated path (see the RelicModel._status/StackCount/IsWax/IsMelted entries above), and can never end up inconsistent with this counter's own restored value, which was captured from the exact same relic instance at the exact same instant. MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Models.Relics.Unsettl.reason: FIXED — this entry previously described the pre-fix hole and is kept as the record of it. It DOES mutate mid-combat: DoubledPowers.Add(power) fires from the power-application hook (UnsettlingLamp.cs:107), is cleared only at BeforeCombatStart (:66) and AfterCombatEnd (:155), and the already-doubled check (:171) reads it, so a stale entry would refuse to double a power again after an undo. Originally that happened, because Shadow() was MemberwiseClone, which copies reference-typed fields by reference: the shadow and the live relic shared one List and the field was never actually snapshotted. Shadow() now deep-copies container fields — copy constructor for collections, Array.Clone() for arrays (StateSnapshot.cs:313-375) — and List<PowerModel> has a (IEnumerable<T>) copy constructor, so the shadow holds its own list and CopyMutableFields assigns that back on restore. Only fields whose runtime type has no usable copy constructor stay shared, which in practice is DynamicVarSet alone (captured separately); a headless 150-combat run reported copied=92 shared=29282 with DynamicVarSet as the sole occupant of the shared count. Element identity is still shared (shallow copy), which is correct here: the list holds live PowerModel references that the restore re-binds anyway. Note this entry was itself the source of a later misreading — a reviewer took the stale text at face value and reported the bug as still live.

Plain bool backing a private property (UnsettlingLamp.cs:50-61) that only gates re-triggering within BeforePowerAmountChanged/ModifyPowerAmountGivenMultiplicative (UnsettlingLamp.cs:78, 121) and is reset alongside TriggeringCard/DoubledPowers at BeforeCombatStart/AfterCombatEnd (UnsettlingLamp.cs:63-70, 152-159). Unlike its sibling _doubledPowers (already flagged FINDING above: a List<PowerModel> aliased by Shadow()'s shallow MemberwiseClone, so it never actually gets reset by an undo), this field IS a value type -- Shadow() captures it by value and CopyMutableFields restores exactly what it was at snapshot time, so on its own it restores correctly. Flagging for awareness only: because _doubledPowers stays stuck at its live (unrolled-back) contents while this field and TriggeringCard correctly roll back to 'not yet triggered', a restore mid-trigger could let BeforePowerAmountChanged re-add a power to the already -stale _doubledPowers list -- that compounding failure mode belongs entirely to _doubledPowers's already-reported aliasing bug, not to this field.
Same as Vambrace._triggeringCard: a CardModel reference, reference-compared only, and card identity is preserved across restore.
